title: Are Affiliate Programs Legit or Scams? How to Tell the Difference Before You Sign Up
summary: Affiliate programs are a legitimate business model, but scams hide inside them. Use these red flags and a simple scorecard to tell a real program from a scam before you sign up.
body_markdown:
## Affiliate Programs Are Legitimate, but Each Program Needs Its Own Check


Affiliate programs are legitimate when a business pays partners for qualifying referrals under clear, written terms. The business model does not guarantee that every offer is trustworthy: verify the merchant, product, tracking method, and payout rules before promoting anything.


### How affiliate marketing works: CPS, CPA, CPL, and CPC


An affiliate shares a tracked link, code, or other referral method. If a qualifying action follows, the program attributes it to that affiliate and applies the agreed payment model. CPS pays for a sale, CPA for a specified action, CPL for a qualified lead, and CPC for a click. The qualifying event matters: a sale may be canceled, a lead may need validation, and a click may not count if it fails the program’s rules.


### From early online referrals to Amazon Associates and today’s programs


Affiliate marketing developed from online referrals into a structured channel for tracking and paying publishers. Amazon Associates launched in July 1996, helping make product links and referral commissions familiar to online publishers. Today, programs may run through a merchant’s own system or an affiliate platform, with dashboards for clicks, orders, commissions, and payout status.


### Why similar-looking networks can offer very different terms


A familiar dashboard does not mean two programs share the same rules. Commission rates, attribution windows, eligible countries, return handling, payment thresholds, and prohibited promotional methods can all differ. Read the terms for your specific offer, not just the platform description. Reacher Affiliate Program is one example of a named referral offer; its published terms state: Unlimited referrals and referral payouts for up to 12 months. The program also states: 20% commission per Reacher client referral, per month.


### What beginners can realistically expect to earn


There is no standard beginner income. Earnings depend on audience trust, offer fit, qualified traffic, conversion rates, and written commission rules. A high advertised rate can still produce little income if the offer does not suit your audience or referrals do not convert. Treat early earnings as uncertain, and do not spend money on promotion until you understand the offer and its advertising restrictions.
